name: Li-ion Battery Current-Collector Foils: Aluminium & Copper Foil Localisation
scope: Battery-grade aluminium (cathode) and copper (anode) current-collector foil in India: demand, import dependence, policy (battery-component scheme, anti-dumping duty) and the listed companies building capacity.

summary.one_line: India imports an estimated 80-85% of its battery foil. DGTR has recommended five more years of anti-dumping duty on aluminium foil, and the Finance Ministry has until 15 Dec 2026 to decide. Hindalco has commissioned capacity and SRF has approved a plant, but demand depends on gigafactories that are mostly not built, and foil is a small revenue line for every listed producer.
key_points: IndexBox (May 2026) estimates imports cover 80-85% of India's battery-foil demand in 2026. China supplies 50-55% of import volume, Japan 20-25% and South Korea 10-15%. IndexBox projects 18-22% CAGR over 2026-2035, to 25,000-35,000 t and INR 2,500-4,000 cr by 2035 (S1).

New this edition: DGTR has recommended continuing the anti-dumping duty on aluminium foil of 80 microns and below from China, Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia for five years, at USD 93.53-976.99 per tonne. The Finance Ministry takes the final decision (S22). The existing duty runs until 15 Dec 2026 (S15).

Hindalco commissioned India's first battery-grade aluminium foil facility in Odisha on 27 Jan 2026. It is designed to support up to 100 GWh of cells (S3), and the product page gives 25,000 t of annual capacity (S4). The board meets on 6 Nov 2026 to approve Q2 FY27 results (S25).

SRF's board approved a roughly Rs 600 cr battery-foil plant at SRF Altech's Jetapur (MP) site on 21 Oct 2026. It will be built in two phases of about Rs 300 cr each, with Phase I (12,000 MTPA) due by 30 Sep 2028 and Phase II by 30 Sep 2030 (S6). The plant targets lithium-ion and sodium-ion cells (S7).

Shyam Metalics has still not disclosed any battery-foil sales. Its 18,000 tpa Sambalpur foil plant serves packaging, pharma and industrial uses (S13). Aluminium-foil volumes fell about 19.1% year on year in Sep 2026 (S23).

The roughly Rs 12,000-13,000 cr battery-materials scheme covers cathode, anode, separator, copper foil and electrolyte, but not aluminium foil (S9, S10). Searches this week found no report of EFC or Cabinet approval (S9).

No listed Indian company produces copper battery foil yet. Hindalco holds a Nippon Denkai technology licence for electrodeposited copper foil (S11), but none of its company documents reviewed give a copper-foil capacity.

Demand is lagging. Of 50 GWh under ACC-PLI, 40 GWh has been awarded, but only 1 GWh had been commissioned as of Mar 2026 (S17). IndexBox's 2030 demand estimate of 12,000-16,000 t (S1) is below Hindalco's capacity alone (S4).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: If the Finance Ministry accepts DGTR's recommendation, Hindalco, SRF Altech and Shyam Metalics' subsidiary Shyam Sel and Power keep five more years of duty protection. All three were applicants in the sunset review (S22).
Hindalco is first mover: its plant is commissioned and fed directly from its own FRP complex (S3). It says it serves battery-foil customers in Europe, the USA, Asia and India (S4).
SRF is building on an existing aluminium-foil platform at Jetapur, approved in 2022 at 21,000 MTPA (S8). Its Performance Films & Foil segment grew 51% to Rs 2,122 cr in Q2 FY27 (S7).
Sodium-ion cells use aluminium foil on both electrodes and need an estimated 700-1,000 t per GWh, against 350-500 t for lithium-ion (S16). SRF has explicitly targeted sodium-ion (S7).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Announced aluminium-foil capacity runs ahead of near-term domestic demand. Hindalco's 25,000 t (S4) plus SRF's 12,000 t Phase I (S6) compares with IndexBox's 12,000-16,000 t for 2030 (S1). Hindalco's own forecast is 40,000 t by 2030 (S5).

The duty decision is still open. DGTR has only recommended continuation, and if the Finance Ministry does not notify it, the duty lapses after 15 Dec 2026 (S15, S22). China supplies 50-55% of India's battery-foil imports (S1).
Foil is immaterial to group revenue. IndexBox's entire 2035 Indian market of INR 2,500-4,000 cr (S1) equals about 3-5% of Hindalco's Q1 FY27 quarterly revenue of Rs 84,825 cr (S21).
Gigafactories are delayed: only 1 GWh of 40 GWh awarded had been commissioned by Mar 2026 (S17). Qualification takes a minimum of a few months per sample across several stages (S2).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: The Finance Ministry customs notification on aluminium-foil anti-dumping duty, due before 15 Dec 2026 (S15, S22).
Hindalco's Q2 FY27 results on 6 Nov 2026, for battery-foil utilisation, named cell-maker qualifications and any copper-foil update (S25).
EFC and Cabinet approval of the battery-materials scheme, and whether aluminium foil is added (S9, S10).
Whether Shyam Metalics discloses battery-foil volumes or customers in its monthly sales releases (S23, S24).

sections.title: What battery foil is and why India imports it

blocks.text: In a lithium-ion cell, aluminium foil is the cathode current collector and copper foil is the anode current collector (S2, S9). IndexBox gives typical aluminium battery foil as 12-15 µm thick, with thinning targets of 12-15 µm for aluminium and 6 µm and below for copper. Standard electrodeposited copper is 8-10 µm, and ultra-thin 6 µm copper carries a ±1 µm tolerance (S1). Swarajya puts electrodeposited copper foil at 4.5-8 µm (S9). Chinese industry sources say power-battery aluminium foil is mostly 20, 15, 13 or 12 µm, and moving toward 10 µm and below (S16). Hindalco has developed four battery-grade alloys, including AA1100 and AA1060 (S4).

Qualification is set by the customer. Hindalco says each sample needs a minimum of a few months of testing across several stages (S2). IndexBox says buyers expect certificates covering tensile strength, elongation, surface roughness and thickness uniformity. It adds that existing small-scale domestic foil generally fails battery-electrode specifications for thickness tolerance, roughness and ductility (S1).

blocks.text: The ~4-5% bill-of-materials figure comes from Hindalco, which is a producer (S2). A Chinese trade source puts aluminium foil alone at 1.5-2.0% of Li-ion cost (S16). Neither source explains its basis, so both are shown and treated as indicative only.

IndexBox (report updated 1 May 2026) estimates that imports meet 80-85% of India's battery-foil demand in 2026. China supplies 50-55% of import volume, Japan 20-25% and South Korea 10-15% (S1). Its forecast is 12,000-16,000 t by 2030 and 25,000-35,000 t (INR 2,500-4,000 cr) by 2035, with a bull case above 40,000 t and a bear case of 15,000-18,000 t (S1). Hindalco's own forecast is higher, at 40,000 t of battery-grade aluminium-foil demand by 2030 (S5).

Downstream demand depends on cell plants. Under ACC-PLI (outlay INR 18,100 cr), 40 GWh of the 50 GWh target had been awarded by Mar 2026: Ola Electric 20 GWh, Reliance New Energy 15 GWh and Rajesh Exports 5 GWh. Only Ola's 1 GWh had been commissioned (S17). India imported USD 4.93 bn of lithium-ion batteries in 2025-26, 93.79% of it from China (S9).

subsections.title: Trade protection and the battery-materials scheme

items: Anti-dumping duty (updated): DGTR has recommended a five-year continuation of duties of USD 93.53-976.99 per tonne on aluminium foil of 80 microns and below from China, Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia. The Finance Ministry takes the final decision. The duty was first imposed in Sep 2021 (S22).

The sunset-review applicants were Hindalco, LSKB Aluminium Foils, Raviraj Foils, Shree Venkateshwara Electrocast, Shyam Sel and Power, and SRF Altech (S22). The existing duty was extended to 15 Dec 2026 while the review was completed (S15).
Battery-materials scheme size: about Rs 12,000 cr according to Outlook Business, citing The Economic Times in Jun 2026 (S10), or about Rs 12,000-13,000 cr according to Swarajya (S9).
Scheme scope: cathode, anode, separator, copper foil and electrolyte (S9, S10). Neither source lists aluminium foil, and in May 2025 Hindalco said no PLI covered its aluminium-foil project (S2).

Scheme status: Swarajya reported it moving from the Ministry of Heavy Industries to the finance ministry's Expenditure Finance Committee, and not yet notified (S9). This week's searches found no later approval.

blocks.text: Correction to last week's edition: the anti-dumping review is not just pending. DGTR has already recommended continuing the duty (S22), so the open risk is now the Finance Ministry's notification before 15 Dec 2026 (S15). Aluminium-foil makers are not named beneficiaries of the battery-materials scheme (S9, S10).

subsections.title: Hindalco: commissioned, but small relative to the group

blocks.text: Hindalco says the battery-grade aluminium foil facility it commissioned on 27 Jan 2026 is India's first. It draws input directly from the 1.7 lakh tpa FRP complex (Rs 4,500 cr combined) and is designed to support up to 100 GWh of cells (S3). The product page cites 25,000 t of annual capacity, a 2,400 t customer-qualification line near Nagpur, and an upgraded Mouda foil mill with a battery slitter and test labs (S4). Hindalco has not named any qualified cell makers, saying only that it supplies customers in Europe, the USA, Asia and India (S4). Its Q1 FY27 update lists the plant among commissioned projects but gives no volumes (S21). A results preview says Hindalco's additional Rs 50,000 cr pipeline under evaluation includes new FRP and battery-foil facilities in Odisha (S25).

Materiality is low. Hindalco's Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue was Rs 84,825 cr (S21). IndexBox's entire 2035 Indian battery-foil market of INR 2,500-4,000 cr (S1) equals about 3-5% of one quarter of that revenue (our arithmetic). On copper foil, Nippon Denkai signed a technology licence with Hindalco for electrodeposited Li-ion copper foil in India, with royalties tied to Hindalco's sales (S11). ICICI Direct says Hindalco is setting up a battery copper-foil plant (S10). In May 2025 Hindalco itself described copper foil as early-stage (S2).

SRF's 21 Oct 2026 approval is a project under its wholly owned subsidiary SRF Altech at the existing Jetapur, MP site, funded through debt and internal accruals. The filing frames it as adding future-ready, value-added products for energy storage and EVs (S6). It extends the 21,000 MTPA aluminium-foil plant approved in Jan 2022 for Rs 425 cr (S8). In Q2 FY27 SRF's Performance Films & Foil segment revenue rose 51% to Rs 2,122 cr, against consolidated revenue of Rs 4,904 cr (S7).

Shyam Metalics announced battery-grade foil in Sep 2023, with 12-20 µm product validated by third-party labs, but gave no battery-specific capacity (S12). Its 18,000 tpa Sambalpur foil plant began commercial production on 16 Jul 2026 to serve packaging, pharma and industrial uses (S13). Q1 FY27 foil sales were 5,606 t at a realisation of about INR 4.83 lakh/t (S24), which implies roughly Rs 270 cr of foil revenue in the quarter (our arithmetic). Foil volumes were softer in Q2 FY27 and fell about 19.1% year on year in Sep 2026, although realisations were higher (S23). None of these disclosures separate out battery foil.

No disclosed source confirms commercial battery-foil sales by Shyam Metalics. It stays in the commissioned bucket only because its foil capacity is operating and it claims battery-grade capability (S12, S13, S14).

subsections.title: Has the market priced it in?

blocks.title: Share-price returns to 2 Nov 2026
blocks.source: Source: ICICIdirect quote pages (S18, S19, S20)

blocks.text: Share prices do not track the foil theme. Hindalco is down 12.2% over six months (S18), and SRF is down 19.19% over one year despite the foil approval (S19). Shyam Metalics is up 36.31% over six months (S20) even though its foil volumes are falling (S23). Coverage is thin. ICICI Direct named Hindalco as a potential copper-foil beneficiary in a battery-component note (S10), and our searches found no dedicated broker thematic on 'battery foil stocks' and no broker note specifically on SRF's foil plant.

rows: 80-85% import dependence; 18-22% CAGR over 2026-35; 25,000-35,000 t by 2035; domestic commercial output unlikely before 2028-29; Reliance New Energy and Ola Cell exploring foil backward integration

blocks.text: IndexBox's 'top participants' list names companies such as Exide, Tata AutoComp and Mahindra as foil players. That conflicts with its own text, which says no large-scale domestic foil plant operates, so those names are not used here (S1).

items: Trade: the duty continues only if the Finance Ministry notifies DGTR's recommendation before the current duty ends on 15 Dec 2026 (S15, S22). Chinese copper-foil overcapacity, about 2.1 mn t against about 1 mn t of demand, can depress prices (S9).
Demand timing: 1 GWh of 40 GWh awarded under ACC-PLI had been commissioned by Mar 2026 (S17). IndexBox does not expect domestic commercial output before 2028-29 (S1).
Overcapacity: Hindalco's 25,000 t (S4) plus SRF's 12,000 t (S6) exceeds IndexBox's 2030 demand of 12,000-16,000 t (S1), so producers would need to export.
Qualification: testing takes a minimum of a few months per sample (S2), and no named cell-maker approvals have been disclosed (S4).
Policy: the battery-materials scheme has not been notified, and reported drafts exclude aluminium foil (S9, S10).
Materiality: foil is a small part of revenue for all three producers (S1, S7, S21, S24).

companies.name: Hindalco Industries
companies.role: Commissioned India's first battery-grade aluminium foil facility at Aditya, Odisha, in Jan 2026: 25,000 tpa supporting ~100 GWh, plus a 2,400 t qualification line near Nagpur (S3, S4). Holds a Nippon Denkai licence for electrodeposited copper foil (S11).
companies.impact: First mover, and an applicant for the anti-dumping duty that DGTR has recommended continuing (S22). The only listed name with a copper-foil route into the pending scheme (S10). Foil is immaterial against quarterly revenue of Rs 84,825 cr (S21). Q2 FY27 results are due on 6 Nov 2026 (S25).

companies.name: Shyam Metalics and Energy
companies.role: Aluminium-foil producer. Announced third-party-validated 12-20 µm battery foil in 2023 (S12) and started an 18,000 tpa, 6-40 µm foil plant at Sambalpur in Jul 2026 aimed at packaging, pharma and industrial uses (S13).
companies.impact: Its subsidiary Shyam Sel and Power was an anti-dumping applicant (S22). No battery-foil volumes have been disclosed, and foil volumes fell ~19.1% YoY in Sep 2026 (S23). The stock is up 36.31% over six months (S20).

companies.name: SRF
companies.role: Board approved a ~Rs 600 cr battery aluminium-foil plant through SRF Altech at Jetapur, MP: 12,000 MTPA Phase I by Sep 2028 and Phase II by Sep 2030 (S6), for Li-ion and sodium-ion cells (S7). It builds on a 21,000 MTPA foil plant approved in 2022 (S8).
companies.impact: Adjacent to its Performance Films & Foil segment, whose Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 2,122 cr (S7). SRF Altech was an anti-dumping applicant (S22). Battery revenue starts only from 2028. The stock is down 19.19% over one year (S19).

companies.name: Ola Electric Mobility
companies.role: ACC-PLI beneficiary with 20 GWh awarded, and the only commissioned capacity (1 GWh) as of Mar 2026 (S17). IndexBox says Ola Cell Technologies is exploring backward integration into foil (S1).
companies.impact: Its cell ramp-up is the largest single driver of domestic foil demand, and any in-house foil plan would compete with merchant suppliers (S1, S17).

companies.name: Reliance Industries
companies.role: Reliance New Energy holds 15 GWh under ACC-PLI (S17), and IndexBox names it as exploring backward integration into foil (S1).
companies.impact: A potential large foil buyer, or a captive producer if it integrates. No company-confirmed foil plan was found (S1, S17).

companies.name: Rajesh Exports
companies.impact: It only adds foil demand once its gigafactory is commissioned, which had not happened as of Mar 2026 (S17).

companies.name: HEG
companies.role: Setting up a graphite anode facility. ICICI Direct sees it as a potential beneficiary of the same battery-materials scheme that covers copper foil (S10).
companies.impact: Adjacent, not a foil maker: scheme notification would move anode and copper-foil names together (S10).

companies.name: Graphite India
companies.role: Signed an MoU with Maharashtra for a synthetic-graphite anode project. ICICI Direct names it as a potential scheme beneficiary (S10).
companies.impact: Adjacent, not a foil maker: exposed to the same scheme-approval timing (S9, S10).

method: Weekly refresh of the 2026-W44 edition, researched on 4 Nov 2026 with web searches and direct page fetches. Changes this week: (1) DGTR's recommendation of a five-year continuation of the aluminium-foil anti-dumping duty, from The Pioneer (24 Sep 2026), which corrects last week's description of the review as pending; (2) Shyam Metalics' Q1 and Q2 FY27 foil volumes and realisations from AlCircle and Univest, based on company sales releases (the NSE sales-release PDF timed out on fetch); (3) Hindalco's 6 Nov 2026 Q2 board meeting and Odisha battery-foil pipeline, from a results preview; (4) share-price returns refreshed from ICICIdirect pages timestamped 2 Nov 2026, which match numbers.json prices. Searches found no EFC or Cabinet approval of the battery-materials scheme, no company-confirmed copper-foil capacity (Swarajya's Waghodia figure is flagged as unconfirmed), and no new listed small-cap battery-foil producer. The other DGTR applicants (LSKB, Raviraj, Shree Venkateshwara) were not confirmed as listed and are not included. Sources dropped as stale or redundant: ChemAnalyst (Mar 2025), DSIJ (2023) and the SMM Dec 2025 price, along with the arithmetic that relied on it. The extra companies are cell makers (foil demand) and battery-materials scheme peers (adjacent), labelled 'other'. 'Our arithmetic' marks simple derived figures. No ratings or price targets.
